body.title: [CLI] ZodError: invalid_union when resuming a conversation - null fileId in generatedFiles breaks schema validation
body.body:
## Description

When attempting to resume an existing conversation via the CLI (using `/resume` in interactive mode or `-c <conversationId>` in non-interactive mode), the CLI throws a `ZodError` with code `invalid_union` and exits without loading the conversation.

A **new conversation works correctly**. The issue is specific to the conversation being resumed.

## Root Cause (identified from the error JSON)

The error occurs at `conversation.content[142][0]`, which is an `agent_message`.

The CLI's Zod schema validation fails because:

> `conversation.content[142][0].actions[19].generatedFiles[0].fileId` is `null`

but the schema expects a `string`.

The union validation then fails entirely because:
- It's not a `user_message` (type mismatch)
- It's not a valid `agent_message` (because `fileId` is `null` instead of `string`)
- It's not a `content_fragment` (type mismatch)

**The fix would be to update the CLI's Zod schema to accept `string | null` for `generatedFiles[x].fileId`.**

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an existing conversation that contains an agent message with a `generatedFiles` entry where `fileId` is `null`
2. Attempt to resume this conversation via the CLI.
3. The CLI returns the `ZodError` JSON below.

## Additional context

- The conversation was originally created in personal space, then moved to a **Pod**, then moved back again to personal space. The error persists even after the move and occurs also on conversations that never created or moved into a Pod.
- `dust logout` + `dust login` did not resolve the issue.
- `dust cache:clear` did not resolve the issue.

## Error JSON

```json
[
  {
    "code": "invalid_union",
    "unionErrors": [
      {
        "issues": [
          {
            "received": "agent_message",
            "code": "invalid_literal",
            "expected": "user_message",
            "path": ["conversation", "content", 142, 0, "type"],
            "message": "Invalid literal value, expected \"user_message\""
          }
        ],
        "name": "ZodError"
      },
      {
        "issues": [
          {
            "code": "invalid_type",
            "expected": "string",
            "received": "null",
            "path": ["conversation", "content", 142, 0, "actions", 19, "generatedFiles", 0, "fileId"],
            "message": "Expected string, received null"
          }
        ],
        "name": "ZodError"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## Environment

- **CLI version**: 0.4.5
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04
- **Node.js version**: 24.18.0

body.title: [front] Data source usage reads agent status from the agents table
body.body:
## Description

Part of moving agent head fields (`status`, `scope`) off `agent_configurations` and onto `agents`.

The usage aggregates in `agent_data_sources.ts` (`getDataSourcesUsageByCategory`, `getDataSourceUsage`, `getDataSourceViewUsage`) filtered on `agent_configurations.status = 'active'`. That also meant "current version only", since saving a version archives the older rows. Their configuration include now includes `AgentModel` with:
- `agents.status = 'active'`
- `agents.currentVersion = agent_configurations.version`

`agent_configurations` is still joined, because tool links point at a configuration row (`agent_mcp_server_configurations.agentConfigurationId`) and `pictureUrl` only exists there. These queries no longer read its `status`.

`getDataSourceViewsUsageByModelIds` now goes through `listActiveConfigurationIdentities` (dust-tt/dust#33726). That function still reads `status` and `scope` from `agent_configurations` and is left for a follow-up, since `agent_triggers.ts` uses it too.

This PR doesn't change the existing visibility behaviour.

## Tests

New test in `lib/api/agent_data_sources.test.ts`. It sets up five agents: one visible, one hidden, one hidden that the member edits, one whose link is only on a superseded version, and one archived. It then checks all four usage functions as an admin and as a member.

## Risk

Low. These are read-only queries and the results are unchanged. Safe to roll back.

body.title: [front] chore: upgrade date-fns to v4
body.body:
## Description

First of three PRs moving `front` from `date-fns-tz` to `@date-fns/tz`, the official date-fns timezone package. `@date-fns/tz` only works with date-fns v4 (on v3, a `TZDate` silently falls back to the host timezone), so this bumps `date-fns` from 3.6 to v4 in `front` and `front-api`.

`front-api` gets its own `date-fns` entry because it loads packages from the root `node_modules` at runtime, which would otherwise keep serving v3 to `front` code. No code changes. No visual change.

## Tests

* `npm run tsgo` passes in `front` and `front-api`.
* The 16 date-related suites (analytics exports, observability, workspace analytics, timezone, activation slots, i18n format, Google Calendar) pass locally: 354 tests.

## Risk

Low. v4 has few breaking changes and the typecheck is clean. Rollback is a revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front` and `front-api`. No migration, no flag.

body.title: [front] refactor(i18n): format hardcoded en-US call sites through the module
body.body:
## Description

Refs dust-tt/tasks#10695.

Sorts the `"en-US"` call sites in UI code (`components/`, `hooks/`, `lib/client/`, `lib/swr/`) and forbids the literal there with the new `noHardcodedEnUsLocale` Grit rule (contract `no-hardcoded-en-us-in-ui`).

- **Numbers, currencies, file sizes, all-numeric dates and times** drop their locale and go through `formatNumber`, `formatCurrency`, `formatFileSize`, `formatDate` and `formatTime`. They follow the format locale, which is the browser's while the `localisation` flag is off.
- **Dates with month or weekday names** pass `getActiveLocale()` explicitly, like the calendar labels of #33783: with the flag off they stay English in an English UI.
- `formatTimestampToFriendlyDate` moves from `lib/utils.ts` to `lib/client/friendly_date.ts` (55 importers updated): `lib/utils.ts` is imported by server code and can't import Lingui. Its only server caller, the archived-skill rename in `skill_resource.ts`, now calls `formatDateTime(…, "en-US")` with the same options.
- `formatConsumptionDate` and `formatWakeUpSidebarLabel` take a required `locale`, for the same reason. Their callers pass `getActiveLocale()`.
- `formatCreditValue` picked "credit" or "credits" by parsing its own formatted output with `replaceAll(",", "")`. It now rounds the number instead.
- The one remaining literal in UI code is a key of the per-locale map in `relative_time.ts`, with a `biome-ignore`. No machine-facing call site (export, API parameter, file name) was found in these directories.

Server code (`lib/api/**`, notifications, providers, email) keeps its `"en-US"`: it isn't covered by the rule.

### Output

| | en-US browser, flag off | fr-FR browser, flag off | fr-FR user, flag on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credits | `1,234.6` | `1 234,6` | `1 234,6` |
| Compact USD | `$1.2K` | `1,2 k $US` | `1,2 k $US` |
| Seat price (EUR) | `€1,234.56` | `1 234,56 €` | `1 234,56 €` |
| File size | `1.5 KB` | `1,5 KB` | `1,5 KB` |
| Numeric date | `09/23/2025` | `23/09/2025` | `23/09/2025` |
| Friendly long date | `September 23, 2025 at 5:37:32 PM` | same | `23 septembre 2025 à 17:37:32` |
| Usage chart date | `Sep 23` | `Sep 23` | `23 sept.` |
| Wake-up label | `Sun` | `Sun` | `dim.` |

### Visible English changes (flag off)

- The `compact` friendly date loses its comma: `Sep, 2025` → `Sep 2025`. The comma was inserted with a string replace, which would have given `sept., 2025` in French.
- Seat prices in non-USD currencies were forced to `fr-FR` formatting. They now follow the browser: an English browser shows `€1,234.56` instead of `1 234,56 €`.

### Known follow-up

`SubscriptionActionButtons` shortens `periodEndLabel` with `split(",")[0]`. With the flag on in French, the date is no longer shortened.

## Tests

- `format.test.ts`: the currency helpers move from "legacy helpers keep their output" to per-locale expectations, and the `compact` friendly date is updated.
- `credits.test.ts`, `amounts.test.ts`: pin the format locale to `en-US`.
- `wakeup_description.test.ts`: passes the locale.

## Risk

Low. With the flag off, only users whose browser isn't en-US see a change, in number and numeric-date formatting. Safe to roll back.

## Deploy Plan

Front only.

body.title: [front] Don't count programmatic usage against the member's own caps
body.body:
## Description

A Slack workflow message resolved to a member (system key + `x-api-user-email`) is programmatic (`slack_workflow`) but carries the member on auth, so its cost was recorded in both the programmatic counters and the member's fair-use / per-user spend-cap counters. `computeAndStoreAgentMessageCredits` now skips the user counters for programmatic usage, and the legacy per-member cap gate now skips programmatic messages, like the fair-use gate already does.

## Tests

New tests in `credit_cost.test.ts` (recording) and `conversation.test.ts` (legacy gate). Both fail without the fix.

## Risk

Low. Programmatic messages sent on behalf of a member no longer use up or check that member's own caps; the programmatic caps still apply. On credit-priced plans, `isUserBlocked` still gates these messages (unchanged).

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front.

body.title: [front] refactor: format dates in a timezone with @date-fns/tz
body.body:
## Description

Every `formatInTimeZone(date, zone, pattern)` call becomes `format(date, pattern, { in: tz(zone) })` from date-fns v4 and `@date-fns/tz`. Outlook rendering renames its local `tz` variable to `timeZones` so it doesn't shadow the imported helper. Zone conversions (`toZonedTime`, `fromZonedTime`, `toDate`) are left for #33917.

One behavior difference: an empty-string timezone used to format as UTC and now throws. Every caller already validates the timezone with `isValidTimezone`, which rejects an empty string, so this can't happen in practice.

## Tests

* Old and new output compared for all 9 patterns in use across 7 zones and 5 instants (DST edges, Samoa's skipped day, Lord Howe's 30 minute DST): 315 of 315 identical

## Risk

Low. Formatting only, with output checked identical. Rollback is a revert.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front` and `front-api` after #33915. No migration, no flag.
